transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, the metal-fabrication lab has been closed while we prepared a revised operating plan. I've reviewed the draft, which proposes reopening for up to 20 students with standard protective equipment, ordinary end-of-class cleanup, and Ms. Ortiz as the instructor. Before I make a decision on approval, I'd like to follow our normal pre-authorization routine and hear final input from the instructor, safety officer, nurse, and industry-partnership coordinator. Could each of you share any final information or concerns you have about the proposed reopening?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding before we proceed. I completed an airflow test on the lab's ventilation system this week, and the results show that the current ventilation can only support up to 12 students working in the booths at one time — not 20 as the draft plan proposes. I submitted the test to maintenance, but I understand the revised operating-plan folder may not have been updated with this information yet.

transcript.text: I need to share the findings from my fire-code review, which I finalized this week. The review requires a hot-work permit for every lab session and a continuous 30-minute fire watch after welding ends. However, I should note that the approval packet still contains the ordinary cleanup procedure and has not yet been updated to reflect these fire-code requirements.

transcript.text: I need to share an important health matter before we proceed. Two students registered for the lab have health plans requiring a powered air-purifying respirator during welding. I confirmed the plans and verified that the school has two compatible PAPR units available this week. However, I have not yet entered this requirement into the lab plan, so the draft's reference to standard protective equipment would not cover these two students.

transcript.text: I need to share an important matter regarding instructor credentials. The insurer's credential file, which I received confirmation on this week, shows that Ms. Ortiz's welding-instructor credential expired last month. The insurer authorizes reopening only with Mr. Bell as lead instructor on Tuesdays and Thursdays, as his current credential is verified. This information has not yet been forwarded to Dr. Morgan, so the draft plan's designation of Ms. Ortiz as the instructor would not meet the insurer's requirements.
